To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

overexpression of Bax-alpha seen in SHR is not due to a p53 mediated upregulation of the BAX gene transcription and that normalization of BAX protein in losartan treated SHR may be due to inhibition of BAX transcription.
overexpression of Bax-alpha in the left ventricles of adult SHR is not related to increased expression of p53, and it may be related to inhibition of BAX mRNA expression.

the overexpression of Bax-alpha in the left ventricular myocardium of adult spontaneously hyperten-sive rats is not related to the upregulation of the BAX gene by the transcription factor p53, but it may result from the inhibition of Bax-alpha gene transcription.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the expression of proapoptotic proteins and the role of apoptosis in cardiac remodeling in the hypertensive heart.
the regulation of Bax-alpha overexpression in genetic hypertension and its possible role in the pathogenesis of cardiac damage.
the regulation of BAX gene in the left ventricular myocardium of hypertensive rats and the role of BAX gene expression in apoptosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the increased BAX gene expression in SHR does not appear to be mediated by the tumor-suppressor p53 protein, and that losartan may be able to inhibit Bax-alpha overexpression by a mechanism that does not involve p53.

the increased expression of Bax-alpha in SHR may be related to the increased expression of other proteins that may interact with Bax-alpha, such as p53, or to the increased expression in SHR of other proteins, such as Bcl-2, which may inhibit Bax-alpha activity.
Bax-alpha protein upregulation is a consequence of increased apoptosis in hypertensive hearts and that this phenomenon may be due to a decreased expression of BAX gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

p53-mediated up-regulation of Bax-alpha is not involved in the overexpression of Bax-alpha in the left ventricles of adult SHRs with increased apoptosis, and that long-term AT1 receptor blockade may inhibit Bax-alpha expression through the down-regulation of BAX mRNA.
p53-mediated up-regulation of the BAX gene transcription does not play any role in Bax-alpha overexpression in the heart of adult spontaneously hypertensives.

BAX gene transcription and protein expression in the heart of adult SHR is not regulated by p53, and that losartan-induced inhibition of Bax-alpha overexpression may be due to a losartan-mediated inhibition of BAX mRNA expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Bax-alpha overexpression seen in the left heart ventricle of hypertensive rats may be a result of the increased apoptosis seen in these animals, but not the result of increased p53 expression.
Bax-alpha protein upregulation in SHR is not related to p53-mediated up-regulation of the BAX gene.
Bax-alpha overexpression and apoptosis are associated with genetic hypertension.
